newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bullion to push higher, with dollar weak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullion to push higher, with dollar weak.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Precious metal markets are likely to push higher across the board on Monday, with the weakness in the dollar over-riding short-term technicals, analysts said.
Gold is at a one-month high, and likely to target $350.00, while a strong platinum market is at its highest since late February and seen heading towards $400, they said.
PLATINUM -
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were leading the way in early action, particularly platinum, which had gained some $10 from Friday afternoon levels.
"There was a lot of activity in the yen overnight, and when we came in it (platinum) was up by $10," one trader said.
The dollar fell overnight against the yen to below 118 yen -- the lowest level in nearly four months.
Palladium also pushed up to new two-year highs above $170.00, some $7.00 up from late Friday levels.
The PGMs were also being supported by the tightness in forward rates, as well as the concern over supplies from Russia.
At 0840 GMT platinum was indicated at $395.00/396.00, up $5.00 from Friday.
GOLD -
The market has enjoyed a solid run in recent sessions and this trend is expected to be maintained in the long term, analysts and traders said.
Although there were short-term technical corrective signals, the weakness of the dollar might offset this, some traders said.
"People are watching the yen/dollar, so it could go to $350," one said.
Other analysts saw technical pressure holding sway and a short-term reaction setting in.
"It is a bit overbought at the moment, so it could go back to $343/345, and then resume the uptrend," one European analyst said.
At 0840 GMT gold was indicated at $348.45/348.75, up some $0.70 from late pre-weekend levels.
SILVER-
Prices were also likely to benefit from the general strength in precious metals, with a target in the mid-$4.90s looming. But again chart corrective factors might well come into play.
"Around $4.93/4.95 there will be some resistance, and it could go back down to $4.85 in the short term," the European analyst said.
At 0840 GMT silver was quoted at $4.88/4.90, up from a previous $4.86/4.88.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
